pr_title: Core: Report browser errors in parseXML
pr_body:
### Summary ### Fixes gh-4784 In IE 11 we'd just throw an empty error now, in others - the reported error. We wouldn't include input data in the thrown error anymore. +10 bytes, although I cheated a bit - I also removed an assignment of `xml` to `undefined` in `catch` as any error would happen before the assignment so the variable would already hold the `undefined` value. Without this optimization, it'd be +13 bytes. That +10 can be changed to -3 if we just call: ```js jQuery.error( parserErrorElem && parserErrorElem.textContent ) ``` but that has two issues. Here's the returned element `parsererror` (after pretty-printing) in Blink & WebKit: ```xml

This page contains the following errors:

error on line 14 at column 9: Opening and ending tag mismatch: th line 0 and tr

Below is a rendering of the page up to the first error.

 ``` and here's the one in Gecko: ```xml XML Parsing Error: mismatched tag. Expected: </th>. Location: http://sandbox.l/test.xhtml Line Number 14, Column 6: </tr>\n--------------------------^ ``` If we just print `textContent`, in Chrome the text will miss spaces in some places: ``` This page contains the following errors:error on line 14 at column 9: Opening and ending tag mismatch: th line 0 and tr Below is a rendering of the page up to the first error. ``` That may not be enough a reason to add bytes but here's what ends up in Firefox: ``` XML Parsing Error: mismatched tag. Expected: . Location: http://sandbox.l/test.xhtml Line Number 14, Column 6: --------------------------^ ``` Firefox prints ASCII art which is misaligned now. With the code from this PR, here's what gets printed: ``` XML Parsing Error: mismatched tag. Expected: . Location: http://sandbox.l/test.html Line Number 14, Column 6: --------------------------^ ``` On the other hand, it actually uses tabs to pad `` and the alignment depends on tab being rendered as 8 characters... So maybe we can give up on that. **EDIT:** Actually, this will mostly be printed in the DevTools of the respective browser, here: Firefox. So it should show up correctly in the console. Let's make a decision at the next meeting. ### Checklist ### * [x] All authors have signed the CLA at https://cla.js.foundation/jquery/jquery * [x] New tests have been added to show the fix or feature works * [x] Grunt build and unit tests pass locally with these changes * ~~If needed, a docs issue/PR was created at https://github.com/jquery/api.jquery.com~~
pr_comments: I updated the PR with proposed changes; unfortunately, now it's at +25 bytes.
@dmethvin does the current version look good to you?

issue_context.title: jQuery.parseXML should add detailed information about parse errors
issue_context.body:
### Description ###
If an invalid XML is passed to jQuery.parseXML, currently the thrown parse error only contain the input data but not the error reason.
However the internally created XML document contains the parser errors in the element parsererror as innerText and could be added. This is helpful for debugging errors in XML files

### Link to test case ###
https://jsfiddle.net/o678xuz3/
comments: Thanks for the report. However, the test case attached doesn't work, it even doesn't include jQuery. Please share a test case where the issue and what you'd expect instead can be reproduced.

I'm sorry I have not described the testcase properly.
It is using jQuery which is available implicitely and it uses the jQuery.parseXML. It logs the error message that is raised by the parser to the console.
Additionally it logs the error which the internally used XML parser produces and which should be returned.

What do you propose us to change? `jQuery.parseXML` returns the parsed XML and doesn't crash in case of errors. Do you propose that an error we log to the console contained contents of `xml.getElementsByTagName( "parsererror" )` as well?
I propose to add the xml.getElementsByTagName( "parsererror" )[0].innerText to the text of the thrown Error.
I like this idea. I'd much prefer to either show the parserror content (with provided snippet) or a generic message without trying to add the data to the string.

review_comments: I guess the `!xml` check should be around `xml.getElementsByTagName` instead?
